title: Writing C for the Web in 2026 Isn't Insane. It Might Be the Future
why_read: A thought-provoking essay on building a modern commercial web app in plain C served via CGI, appealing to those interested in minimalist, dependency-free software design.
analysis: The piece discusses a real shipping product built entirely in C using CGI, a very old but simple web serving technology, as a reaction against modern supply-chain risk and dependency bloat. It's less about new technical mechanics and more a philosophical argument for simplicity and auditability in an era of AI-generated code and complex toolchains. Readers interested in minimalist engineering philosophy will find it engaging, though it offers limited concrete new technical detail itself.
